analysis.one_liner: Adani Green Energy develops and operates large-scale solar, wind and hybrid power plants across India, selling electricity to state utilities and corporates under long-term contracts.
analysis.whats_happening: The board meets on 21 October 2026 to approve Q2/H1 FY27 results, with the analyst call on 22 October - this falls within the next few days. The stock fell about 7% on 8 October 2026 amid broader weakness in Adani group shares. Two overhangs have cleared this year: the US DOJ dropped its bribery case against group entities in August 2026 after earlier SEC ($18m) and OFAC ($275m) settlements, and SEBI closed its Hindenburg-era disclosure probe against five Adani companies (including this one) for a token ₹45.5 lakh settlement in September 2026, without any admission of guilt.
analysis.plain_terms: This is India's largest listed pure-play renewable power generator, and it is genuinely growing - capacity is up roughly a quarter year-on-year and revenue is climbing at double digits. The tension is that the market is paying a very rich price (over 100 times earnings) for that growth, while the company carries a large pile of debt to fund the power plants it keeps building. If growth or margins slip even slightly, a stock priced this richly has a long way to fall - and one recent quarter where profit nearly vanished is a reminder that the numbers can be lumpy.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026): revenue ₹4,431 cr (+16.6% YoY), EBITDA ₹3,985 cr (+9.9% YoY, ~90% margin), net profit ₹983 cr (+19.3% YoY), energy sold up 30% YoY. That followed a very weak Q3 FY26 (December 2025) where revenue was ₹2,618 cr but net profit was only about ₹5 cr - essentially flat - versus ₹644 cr the quarter before; the cause is not verified here, so treat this swing as a flag rather than a trend. FY26 full year: revenue ₹11,602 cr (+22%), EBITDA ₹10,865 cr (+23%, ~91% margin), with a record 5.1 GW of new capacity added. On the Q1 FY27 call, management guided to ₹42,000 cr of FY27 capex, 5 GW of greenfield additions, and flagged that grid curtailment is currently cutting EBITDA by 5-7%, expected to ease as new transmission capacity comes online later in 2026.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 56.2% from its April 2022 peak of ₹2,970.5, and there is no split, bonus or demerger in the data to explain this away - it is a genuine de-rating, not a corporate-action illusion. Over 1 year it is up 22.8% (well ahead of the Nifty's -9.53% and the peer's -10.14%), and over 3 years it is up 37.25% versus the Nifty's 16.83%. But over 5 years the return is just 8.17%, far behind the Nifty's 25.27% - the business has grown steadily through this period, but the stock was priced for a different world at the 2022 peak and has spent years unwinding that.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 111x and a price-to-book of about 10.7x, this is an expensive stock by any conventional measure. Why it is expensive: the market is pricing in a long runway of capacity growth toward management's 50 GW by FY30 target, high (~90%) operating margins locked in by long-term power contracts, and now reduced legal/regulatory risk after the DOJ and SEBI matters closed. Whether that expense is justified is a separate question - current returns on capital (ROCE 7.39%, ROE 11.4%) are modest and do not themselves support a 111x multiple; the valuation rests almost entirely on execution of future growth, not today's earnings.
analysis.growth_read: This is volume-led growth, not margin-led. Operational capacity rose to 20,763 MW (+24% YoY) and units sold were up 30% YoY in the latest quarter, while operating margins have stayed roughly flat in the 90% band for several quarters. Revenue and EBITDA growth (16-23% YoY) is running somewhat behind capacity growth, which is consistent with new plants still ramping up and with the curtailment drag management itself flagged - worth watching whether growth converts fully once that eases.
analysis.health_read: Operating margins are very high (~90%), so on paper cash generation from existing assets looks strong, but the business is heavily leveraged - total borrowings were around ₹1.03 lakh cr against total assets of ₹1.43 lakh cr as of March 2026, with net debt disclosed at roughly ₹91,000-92,000 cr (sources vary) and about 5.6x run-rate EBITDA per management's own Q1 FY27 disclosure. The dominant risk here is financial (leverage and refinancing risk on a capital-intensive build-out), not operating risk, given the high and stable margins. The near-zero profit in the December 2025 quarter is unexplained in available sources and should be checked directly against the company's filings before drawing conclusions.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (via Adani Trading Services LLP and the S.B. Adani Family Trust) held 62.43% as of September 2026, with 0% pledged - no encumbrance currently disclosed. TotalEnergies remains a large strategic holder but has trimmed its stake from 18.99% to about 17.25% via a block sale, with some reports of plans to sell further; GQG Partners' holding dipped slightly to 4.50% through what is described as an in-kind fund redemption rather than an outright exit. QIA's current position could not be verified in available sources - Not verified, check on Screener or the latest shareholding filing.
strengths: Operational renewable capacity at 20,763 MW, up 24% YoY, with a record 5.1 GW added in FY26 alone
Operating margins held near 90% through FY26 and into Q1 FY27 despite scale-up
Zero promoter pledging disclosed as of the latest filing
Two major legal overhangs (US DOJ case, SEBI Hindenburg probe) closed in 2026 without findings of guilt
watchpoints: Valuation at ~111x earnings and ~10.7x book prices in flawless execution of the 50 GW by FY30 target
Net debt of roughly ₹91,000-92,000 cr, about 5.6x run-rate EBITDA by management's own account
Management-flagged grid curtailment currently cutting EBITDA by 5-7%, with the fix dependent on transmission projects not yet operational
Net profit collapsed to near zero (~₹5 cr) in the December 2025 quarter versus ₹644 cr the prior quarter, with no confirmed explanation
analysis.one_thing: The Q2/H1 FY27 results and call on 21-22 October 2026 - specifically whether EBITDA growth is catching up with capacity growth and whether management confirms curtailment is easing, since that is what the current 111x multiple is betting on.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly P&L and valuation ratios cross-checked on Screener.in against Business Standard/Upstox results coverage and broadly agree. Capacity figures and guidance taken from Q1 FY27 earnings call transcripts; DOJ/SEBI case outcomes taken from Reuters, Business Today and Al Jazeera coverage. Not verified: the exact reason for the near-zero Q3 FY26 profit; a single authoritative net debt or debt-to-equity figure (sources ranged from ₹91,252 cr to ₹92,037 cr net debt, with debt/equity cited anywhere from ~4x to ~9.5x depending on definition); and QIA's current shareholding - these should be checked directly against company filings before being cited further.
